presentation_revision_history.prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Square mature premium painterly mythology encyclopedia artwork of the FAIRY QUEEN selecting the specific Irish AOIBHEALL/AIBHELL/AOIVIL WHITE-CAT transformation. Existing fairy-queen research names Aibhell among Irish fairy queens; Mathew Horgan's1839 manuscript printed by Denham Franklin in Journal Cork Historical Archaeological Society1897 pp85-87 describes Aoivil transformed by her sister Clíodhna into a beautiful white cat, seated on a costly throne with crimson cushions in the enchanted cave palace at Castlecor, guarding gold and silver treasures. Show exactly ONE entirely feline WHITE CAT sitting with poised majestic calm on a small antique throne's deep crimson cushion. Full natural feline head with two cat ears, two eyes, cat muzzle and whiskers, one fluffy white feline torso, exactly FOUR cat legs/paws: two upright forepaws together, two naturally folded hind feet visibly separated, ONE long feline tail curled elegantly along the cushion with tip within frame. All feline anatomy coherent, every ear, paw and tail comfortably inside frame. The cat has a dignified sorrowful enchanted-princess gaze, not caricature. Rich ancient underground palace carved into limestone, subtle gilded architectural ornament and a few plain gold/silver coins on stone floor in background; coins carry no text. Soft impossible cave light, forest-green depths and antique gold highlights, crimson cushion small focal colour, luxurious detailed painterly brushwork. Exact fur length/eye colour, throne design and palace decoration are artistic choices; source supplies white cat and costly crimson throne. No human face/body, human hands, fairy wings, crown or costume on cat, horns, second cat, other animal, human companion, harp, weapon, text, letters, border, signature or watermark. It is Aoibheall's named transformed form, not Clíodhna herself and not a generic pet mascot.
